## Historical audit: S0205

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/teacher_self_evolution_human_pilot/tasks/E01_M1_R1/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines and event names in this file; no observation was split across chunks.

**Inferred goal:** construct a sage-green historic interior, possibly matching a visual target. The original task and any reference image are not present, so the intended fidelity cannot be established.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Line 1, `execute`, step 1 | Code constructs a room shell, two arched windows, wardrobe, table, three chairs, lamp and accessories. Multiple objects and furniture parts are explicitly modeled; chair legs, rails and table pedestal are positioned as assemblies, but their visual or geometric connection is not independently verified. Colors approximate wood, cloth and other surfaces; no image textures are specified. Two dining chairs have distinct headings. |
| Lines 3, 5–7, `build_completed`, `render_completed`, `execution_result`, `select` | Build and render returned code 0; the result reports `ok: true` and a saved PNG, then selects step 1. This validates execution, not appearance. |
| Line 8, `execute`, step 2 | The student revises the scene: extends the room behind the camera to avoid visible front edges, moves the camera closer, changes the right chair heading from −35° to −52°, curves window tracery, and attempts an emission material for window meshes. The code also changes an area-light position. The name-based material assignment’s actual effect is not verified in the trace. |
| Lines 10, 12–14, `build_completed`, `render_completed`, `execution_result`, `select` | The revised build and render also return code 0 and `ok: true`; step 2 is selected. No image pixels, comparison, score, or formal task verdict are supplied. |

**Teacher and exploration:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or receipt appears in this student trajectory; adoption of teacher input is therefore unestablished. The two executions and intervening revision are evidence of student-side iterative exploration, but the trace does not show what prompted it or whether the student visually inspected the first render.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Technical execution succeeded twice; semantic correctness and formal success are **unknown**, not proven partial correctness or algorithm failure. There is no empty patch or visible technical interruption. Camera framing, illumination, texture appearance, part contact, occlusion and resemblance to any target remain unresolved because neither render nor reference image is visible. In particular, extending the room was an attempted framing fix, not proof that an edge problem existed or was resolved.

**Lessons:** Transferably, successful rendering and selection do not verify scene fidelity; visual and geometric checks are separate evidence. Task-specific changes—room extension, window emission and chair rotation—document hypotheses about this composition, not demonstrated improvements.
